summary: Sticky pin expiry triggers short cross-region egress with p95 latency spike and billing question
description:
Issue summary:
Customers observe occasional requests from BrightMaps, pinned to eu-west, routing out via us-east for a small window when their 'sticky pin' TTL expires. Impact: transient p95 latency spikes (~650-900ms) and unexpected cross-region egress charges.

Impact:
- BrightMaps reported increased latency for interactive chat during peak times, affecting UX and SLOs for EU traffic.
- They see additional egress billing lines attributable to US region in invoices for the same time windows.

Environment:
- Customer workspace: brightmaps-prod
- API usage: hosted Redwood API (production) calling model redwood/gptj-6b-v2 pinned to eu-west with pin_ttl=3600s and strict_residency=false

Steps to reproduce (customer provided):
1) Create a pinned session to eu-west with pin_ttl set to 3600s.
2) Send sustained low-rate traffic for ~1 hour.
3) Observe around the TTL expiration boundary some requests route to us-east for 10-30s before returning to eu-west.
4) Note latency and check invoice for egress during those windows.

Observed logs/traces (examples provided by customer):
- trace: trace-eu-0a7b3 (2026-03-09T14:12:58Z) p95 820ms route: eu-west -> us-east -> eu-west
- trace: trace-eu-0a7b9 (2026-03-09T15:12:59Z) p95 680ms route: eu-west -> us-east

Customer ask:
- Why did traffic leave eu-west at the TTL boundary?
- Is this expected behavior for pin expiry?
- Can we avoid cross-region egress and the associated cost/latency when a pin expires?

Notes: customer is enterprise and requests both an explanation and a mitigation that doesn't require major architectural changes on their side.
steps_to_reproduce: Pin model to eu-west with pin_ttl=3600s and strict_residency=false
Run low-rate sustained traffic for >1 hour
Watch for TTL boundary (every 3600s) and capture traces and headers
Inspect routing decisions and billing egress for the observed timestamps
investigation_notes:
Initial triage (support): confirmed customer's traces show a short window where requests were routed to us-east. Hypothesis: when a sticky pin expires, smart-routing evaluates capacity and may pick a fallback region; because strict_residency=false, fallback policy allows cross-region selection to satisfy latency/capacity SLOs.

Engineering triage 2026-03-11 (Marco): reviewed router logs and route decision traces. Found that at TTL boundary the edge cache entry for the pin sometimes lags flush by ~5-20s on a small subset of edge nodes. During that lag, the routing decision treats the request as "unpinned" and applies region preference scoring; if us-east had slightly better immediate capacity score, the router issued a temporary route to us-east. Once the pin re-synchronizes (cache rebuild from control plane), subsequent requests return to eu-west.

We also found the control-plane TTL and edge cache TTL were not perfectly aligned for a few customers due to staggered configuration propagation introduced in a recent rollout (PR 4523). The billing records show cross-region egress for the matched timestamps.

Logs/IDs reviewed:
- router-node-7 logs (2026-03-09T14:12:58Z) request-id=rq-0a7b3 matched trace-eu-0a7b3
- control-plane publish event publish-id=pub-1189 for pin update at 2026-03-09T14:12:55Z

Severity assessment: customer-visible latency spike and unexpected egress cost = customer impact. Marking Sev1 and P1.
comments: BrightMaps (Customer): We see a 10-30s window where p95 jumps and our invoice shows US egress. Can you explain?
Lena Park (Support): Thanks for the report — sharing to Eng to investigate routing at TTL boundaries. Please include trace ids and sample headers (you did — thanks).
Marco Hernandez (Eng): I've reproduced similar behavior in internal test where control-plane propagation lagged behind edge cache expiry. Filing engineering follow-up and temporary mitigations.
BrightMaps: We need a workaround we can apply quickly. Long TTL isn't ideal for our use case because we want some churn.

Marco: Short-term workaround: set strict_residency=true on the pin to forbid fallback to other regions. Alternatively, increase pin_ttl slightly (e.g., +30s) to avoid hitting edge-control boundary during churn windows. We're working on a server-side fix to align TTLs and add routing guard checks.
resolution: In progress: temporary workarounds shared with customer (strict_residency=true or extend pin_ttl by buffer). Engineering change planned: ensure control-plane publish completes before edge cache eviction by adding a pre-eviction guard and a metric to surface pin-expiry misalignments. Target PR created: github.com/redwood/repo/pull/4523. Planned rollout: canary 2026-03-15, full rollout 2026-03-18 if canary shows no regressions. Billing team will review impacted invoices after fix. Customer offered monitoring dashboard for pin-expiry anomalies.
resolution_notes:
Assigned to Marco Hernandez for engineering fix. Action items:
- [ENG] Add pre-eviction check in edge cache (PR 4523)
- [ENG] Add metric and alert for pin-expiry misalignment
- [SUPPORT] Offer customer immediate flag strict_residency toggle and advise on pin_ttl buffer
- [BILLING] Correlate and, if validated, credit the egress for windows impacted by this bug (pending internal review)
- [DOCS] Update routing FAQ to document pin expiry behavior and recommended best practices
customer_communication_plan: Support will follow up 2026-03-12 with timeline for engineering fix and offer temporary config change. If fix is delayed, propose credit for verified egress overage windows; schedule a 30-min review call with BrightMaps by 2026-03-13.
